title: Tutorial: Marascuilo Procedure
text: Let’s create sample dataset representing survey specific opinion across three different cities:
code: df_ejemplo <- data.frame(   City = c(rep("Cordoba", 150), rep("Villa Maria", 75), rep("Rio IV", 75)),   Opinion = c(     rep("Agree", 115), rep("Disagree", 35),     rep("Agree", 53), rep("Disagree", 22),     rep("Agree", 40), rep("Disagree", 35)   ) )

title: Tutorial: Marascuilo Procedure
text: use marascuilo_test() function. need specify dataset, grouping column, response column, specific value represents “success” (case, “Agree”).
code: resultados <- marascuilo_test(   df = df_ejemplo,    col_grupo = "City",    col_respuesta = "Opinion",    valor_exito = "Agree" )

title: Tutorial: Marascuilo Procedure
text: package uses custom S3 class architecture, can simply print object see results comparisons statistically significant: visually interpret results, use autoplot() function. automatically generate ggplot2 chart comparing absolute differences critical ranges pair:
code: resultados #>  #> --- Marascuilo Procedure Results --- #>  #>                               Pair Absolute_Diff Critical_Range    Significance #> Cordoba...1      Cordoba vs Rio IV        0.2333         0.1644     Significant #> Cordoba...2 Cordoba vs Villa Maria        0.0600         0.1540 Not Significant #> Rio IV       Rio IV vs Villa Maria        0.1733         0.1909 Not Significant #>  #> ------------------------------------ ggplot2::autoplot(resultados)

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Proportions Comparison
text: basic example shows solve common problem using package’s generic methods:
code: library(TFGproject) library(ggplot2)  # 1. Create a sample dataset df_ejemplo <- data.frame(   Ciudad = c(rep("Cordoba", 150), rep("Villa Maria", 75), rep("Rio IV", 75)),   Opinion = c(     rep("De acuerdo", 115), rep("En desacuerdo", 35),     rep("De acuerdo", 53), rep("En desacuerdo", 22),     rep("De acuerdo", 40), rep("En desacuerdo", 35)   ) )  # 2. Run the Marascuilo test resultados <- marascuilo_test(   df = df_ejemplo,    col_grupo = "Ciudad",    col_respuesta = "Opinion",    valor_exito = "De acuerdo" )  # 3. Print the results (using the custom print method) resultados #>  #> --- Marascuilo Procedure Results --- #>  #>                               Pair Absolute_Diff Critical_Range    Significance #> Cordoba...1      Cordoba vs Rio IV        0.2333         0.1644     Significant #> Cordoba...2 Cordoba vs Villa Maria        0.0600         0.1540 Not Significant #> Rio IV       Rio IV vs Villa Maria        0.1733         0.1909 Not Significant #>  #> ------------------------------------  # 4. Visualize the comparisons (using the autoplot method) autoplot(resultados)

what: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
text: Computes evaluates possible pairwise comparisons among proportions across multiple independent groups raw dataset. Following statistically significant global test homogeneity, procedure identifies specific pairs proportions differ significantly controlling overall family-wise error rate.

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
text: df data.frame containing raw categorical data. col_grupo Character string specifying column name defines categories/groups. col_respuesta Character string specifying column name responses (e.g., agree/disagree). valor_exito Character string indicating specific value col_respuesta considered statistical success. alpha Numeric value indicating significance level (default 0.05).

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
text: object S3 class marascuilo (inheriting data.frame) containing pairwise comparisons four columns: Pair, Absolute_Diff, Critical_Range, Significance.

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
text: pair groups \(\) \(j\), mathematical procedure compares observed absolute difference sample proportions, \(|\hat{p}_i - \hat{p}_j|\), critical range \(r_{ij}\) defined : $$r_{ij} = \sqrt{\chi^2_{1-\alpha, df}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_i(1-\hat{p}_i)}{n_i} + \frac{\hat{p}_j(1-\hat{p}_j)}{n_j}}$$ \(\chi^2_{1-\alpha, df}\) critical value chi-square distribution \(n_i, n_j\) respective sample sizes group. pairwise comparison declared statistically significant \(|\hat{p}_i - \hat{p}_j| > r_{ij}\).

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
text: Marascuilo, L. . (1966). Large-sample multiple comparisons. Psychological Bulletin, 65(5), 280-290. NIST/SEMATECH (2012). e-Handbook Statistical Methods, Section 7.4.7.4 (Marascuilo procedure). National Institute Standards Technology.

title: Marascuilo Procedure for Multiple Comparisons of Proportions — marascuilo_test
code: library(ggplot2) df_ejemplo <- data.frame(   City = c(rep("Cordoba", 150), rep("Villa Maria", 75), rep("Rio IV", 75)),   Opinion = c(     rep("Agree", 115), rep("Disagree", 35),     rep("Agree", 53), rep("Disagree", 22),     rep("Agree", 40), rep("Disagree", 35)   ) ) resultados <- marascuilo_test(df_ejemplo, "City", "Opinion", "Agree") print(resultados) #>  #> --- Marascuilo Procedure Results --- #>  #>                               Pair Absolute_Diff Critical_Range    Significance #> Cordoba...1      Cordoba vs Rio IV        0.2333         0.1644     Significant #> Cordoba...2 Cordoba vs Villa Maria        0.0600         0.1540 Not Significant #> Rio IV       Rio IV vs Villa Maria        0.1733         0.1909 Not Significant #>  #> ------------------------------------ ggplot2::autoplot(resultados)
